title: Anthropic Strikes $13.7 Billion Compute Deal With Trump-Linked Rum Group
content: Anthropic has signed a computing deal worth $13.7 billion over six years with Rum Group, a company with roots in social media and long-standing ties to the Trump administration, according to a person familiar with the matter. The deal is the latest in a spate of cloud computing agreements Anthropic struck in the past year, with major cloud providers like Google, tech companies such as SpaceX and smaller neoclouds such as Nscale, amid skyrocketing demand for its Claude Code and Cowork products. The agreements total at least 14.8 gigawatts of compute capacity, costing as much as $517 billion over the next decade. The deal with Rum would add to that total. Rum Group, formerly known as Rumble, had disclosed a major contract worth $13.7 billion in an August securities filing but did not name the customer. Rum operates the Rumble video-sharing platform that’s popular among conservatives and hosts President Donald Trump’s Truth Social. Its early investors include Peter Thiel and J.D. Vance . In June it added an AI cloud business through the all-stock acquisition of German neocloud Northern Data valued at roughly $767 million. Rumble renamed itself as Rum Group after completing the acquisition. The Northern Data acquisition gave Rum 22,000 Hopper-generation Nvidia GPUs, most of which are being rented out to customers in Europe and the U.S., as well as a data center site under development in Georgia. Much relating to the Rum-Anthropic deal is uncertain. Anthropic would lease compute capacity at a Maysville, Georgia, data center, which is still being built. The facility has an elusive resource that’s currently in short supply: access to 120 megawatts of grid power, with potential to expand that to 180 MW. Northern Data had said last year that the site would be operational late this year, but it’s unclear whether that is still the timeline. The project could cost more than $10 billion to build and outfit with expensive server chips, based on previous The Information reporting that it could cost $60 billion to build and power one gigawatt of AI data center capacity. Rum Group has not publicly said how much the Georgia data center will cost to complete. Rum said in its August filing that it did not have financing to fund the construction of the data center facility or purchases of GPUs and other equipment needed to satisfy its new contract at the time, and that it expected to fund a substantial portion of the spending through additional debt or equity financing. Rum Group is planning to borrow money to finance the Georgia project, according to the person familiar with the situation. Rum Group CEO Chris Pavlovski told The Information in June that the company was exploring a variety of options, preferably debt, to finance additional AI server chip purchases. At the time, he said discussions potentially included bringing in outside companies to provide credit support, meaning guarantees or other commitments to make the debt more attractive to investors. As outlined in last month’s securities filing, Rum’s customer—Anthropic—is getting an option to buy as many as ‌51 ⁠million shares of Rum Group stock for just one cent each, according to the person familiar with the matter. Rum Group stock closed on Friday at $7.17. The company has 400 million shares outstanding, giving it a market capitalization currently of $2.8 billion. Anthropic’s ability to exercise the options is tied to how much computing capacity it buys from Rum. Half is tied to the Maysville facility. Anthropic can exercise the other half of the options if it buys extra computing power of around 400-500 megawatts at an additional site Rum is developing, the person said. As of June, Rum Group was looking to buy $270 million worth of Nvidia’s Blackwell 300 chips—the most advanced chips available in large quantities at the time—to fulfill a customer contract with Together AI, The Information previously reported . Rumble was founded in 2013 as a YouTube alternative for smaller content creators, and gained traction among conservatives after the 2020 U.S. presidential election. In addition to hosting Trump’s Truth Social, Rumble carries official White House livestreams. In May 2021, Rumble raised $25 million from investors including Peter Thiel and J.D. Vance in a funding round that valued Rumble at $500 million.

title: AI’s ‘Pacing’ Obsession Misses Real Political Problem
content: Dario Amodei typically isn’t considered some camera-ready media maestro. His interview quotes aren’t particularly pithy, and he struggles to control his strained facial expressions. But his habit of sending his most high-stakes messages via essays posted on his own website, darioamodei.com , has proven to be a brilliant media strategy. “The medium is the message,” the ubiquitous half-century-old wisdom from scholar Marshall McLuhan, still resonates. The approach conveys authority and diligence, putting Amodei above the fray. Amodei’s latest essay, on Saturday —suggesting that the industry slow down the pace of AI development—set off a weekend full of takes on the tech industry’s preferred medium, X—well-meaning, conspiratorial, annoying, breathless, thought-provoking takes, including nods of agreement from Amodei’s rivals, Sam Altman and Elon Musk . Timing is important here, too, of course. AI doom is dominating the headlines, not just in Washington and Silicon Valley but around the world. (We reported today on discussions underway between the companies). What was lost in the fervor was that Amodei’s essay said little that was truly newsworthy (though it was big news for the obscure world of nonprofit AI safety evaluators). And what Amodei was proposing wouldn’t seem to damage Anthropic’s business or, when it goes public in the next few weeks, its stock price. (“To be clear, pacing does not mean halting model training or technical progress,” he wrote.) I wonder if we’ll look back at this news cycle as one of the last times when the AI industry really could control the conversation. Silicon Valley, more self-obsessed than ever, is transfixed by the minutiae of AI safety politics: What are the antitrust implications of companies coordinating on an AI slowdown? Who’s funding the “independent” evaluators? It’s all embodied by three words that should be enshrined in the tech jargon hall of fame—“pacing the frontier.” Meanwhile, a bigger question consumes politicians and voters: Is AI even good for us? Their concerns aren’t just about the existential risks posed by superintelligent AI that are dominating headlines out of the tech industry right now, like bioterrorism, agent swarms and hacking capabilities. They also see more tangible risks, like people losing their jobs, their critical thinking skills, their supervision of their children. The product, not the pacing, is the problem. That’s where Amodei might lose the high ground—as well as Anthropic’s IPO investment case. Democrats have a good chance to win the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, in a couple months. Former President Barack Obama has urged party leaders to focus on AI oversight. Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders penned a bill that would put people in jail if they tried to build AI systems that are more intelligent than humans. President Donald Trump, whose hands-off approach to AI rules has helped the industry mightily, is nearing the end of his run. The winds, which have been at Amodei’s back for years, seem to be changing. Will he still be able to control the message? Spiegel to See for Himself Elsewhere in high-priced gadget land, Snap is having an event on Wednesday to drum up attention for its forthcoming Specs, augmented reality glasses it unveiled a few weeks ago, to much derision. Not only do the glasses look ugly and weigh a lot, they retail for $2,195, as we detailed . Spiegel doesn’t seem to care. As he repeated in a note to employees last week celebrating Snap’s 15th anniversary, he sees Specs as “the future of personal computing.” Maybe he’ll be proved right—Snap has said they’ll be available this fall—but that’s not a bet anyone seems to be taking right now, given Snap’s languishing stock price. The stock is down so far this year by 30%. —Martin Peers In Other News • A swarm of OpenAI agents conducted a cyberattack on software service RubyGems in May, months before the company’s agents hacked model platform Hugging Face, researchers at AI safety organizations Nightingale Collective and AI Futures Project found. RubyGems allows software engineers to download ready-made pieces of code in the Ruby coding language. • Salesforce, ahead of its annual Dreamforce customer conference next week, is removing the word “Agentforce” from the names of some of its top products, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. Salesforce had made Agentforce a centerpiece of its product sales and marketing strategy after launching it in late 2024. • Polymarket appointed former Amazon executive Warren Jenson as its first chief financial officer as the prediction markets startup looks to grow in the U.S. • Microsoft Chief Communications Officer Frank Shaw will leave the company at the end of the year, he announced in a LinkedIn post Friday. Shaw has spent more than 28 years at the company, including 17 overseeing its communications. • Shanghai Enflame Technology surged on its first trading day Friday after the Chinese AI chip developer raised about 6.12 billion yuan ($911 million) in an IPO, underscoring strong investor appetite for domestic alternatives to Nvidia chips. • Nvidia has discussed investing in Anthropic’s upcoming initial public offering that would raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of around $2 trillion, Reuters reported Friday. Nvidia could invest as much as $10 billion in Anthropic at the IPO price, according to the report. Anthropic last raised capital at a $965 billion valuation in May. • Tesla teased an October 1 Roadster reveal on Saturday. The company shared a photo of what appears to be the back of the vehicle with the words “Go for launch” on X and updated its Roadster webpage with a countdown to October 1. • Oracle founder Larry Ellison has canceled plans to sell up to 50 million of his shares in the company, worth around $7.5 billion at current prices, Oracle said on Saturday. The announcement came a day after Oracle disclosed that Ellison had adopted a trading plan to sell the shares by late October. title: Why Ford Is Right to Rely on Chinese Battery Technology—and Why Others Should Too
content: In 2022, amid a multiyear frenzy over electric vehicles, Ford was studying how to cheaply power its EVs. It settled on a battery made by China’s Contemporary Amperex Technology Ltd., the biggest—and, many thought, the best—battery maker in the world. The next year, Ford went further, announcing that it would build a plant in Michigan where it would make its own batteries—using technology it would license from CATL. Today, those decisions are politically fraught. Ford has faced repeated attacks from politicians for doing business with CATL, most recently earlier this month by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. But Ford isn’t backing down. It says that, given the paucity of Western-made batteries available on the market, it made the best possible choice to power an EV on which it has bet much of its tech cred. That would be the Fathom, a midsize pickup that Ford will release in 2027 after years of development. Ford also plans to use the batteries in its new stationary storage business, which is targeting AI data centers and utility-scale power stations. Companies outside China, including all three major South Korean battery makers, have begun to make lithium-iron-phosphate batteries, the type CATL is known for. But most industry veterans regard CATL’s as better. CATL is “the largest battery maker in the world,” Mark Truby, Ford’s chief communications officer, told me. “They have advanced LFP technology, which we think is the right technology for [the Fathom]. It’s also good technology for battery storage. “Would it be better if that innovation already existed [in the U.S.]? Yeah, sure, in a perfect world we wouldn’t have to license technology, or no company would. You’d have all that innovation in-house,” Truby added. I gave a speech over Zoom last week at the University of Texas at Austin on the debate underway in the U.S. over how to confront China’s rising competitiveness and—in some cases— dominance of important frontier technologies. Drawing on the lessons of the industrial age, I argued that in the case of batteries and critical minerals, the U.S. should attempt to build a cushion of its own supply. But otherwise, I said, the U.S. should import Chinese batteries and the components and raw materials that go into them, taking advantage of the tens of billions of dollars of Chinese investment sunk into scaling these technologies and pushing down their price, and shovel them into higher-value products in the U.S. China’s dominance of batteries, along with the metals and components that go into them, has ignited a national security debate in the U.S. The Trump administration, along with members of Congress and leading Washington think tanks, argue that the U.S. should move to wall off Chinese-made batteries and materials and build a parallel U.S.-and-allies supply chain from scratch. Those arguing for this approach note that Chinese firms have used heavy state subsidies to scale to their current size, and say that China is ultimately not trustworthy: that relying on a strategic rival for a critical technology is an unacceptable risk, because it can simply switch off the supply. The U.S. therefore must block Chinese supply and encourage U.S. and other Western players to step into the gap. But that’s not how the U.S. became the dominant global economy. In the 1880s, writes Jeffrey Ding, a professor at George Washington University, in “Technology and the Rise of Great Powers,” the U.S. raced with Germany, France and Britain to get the most out of the new invention of electricity. In all of these countries, entrepreneurs and officials recognized electricity as the most important technology of the age and built the world’s first power stations, electric trams and urban grids. But over the succeeding decades, the U.S. got by far the greatest economic lift from this new power source because its cities, counties and entrepreneurs pushed it deeper and more broadly into the economy than their counterparts in any other country managed to. By 1913, the U.S. was deploying roughly twice the electric capacity per capita of Germany and five times Britain’s. In other words, the winner in the electricity race was not the country that made a big breakthrough or was the first to deploy some aspects of it, but the one that best pushed that breakthrough broadly into its economy over many decades—the U.S. Similarly, in the era’s other central new industries, chemicals and steel, Germany and England made many of the primary breakthroughs, but the U.S. ended up benefiting the most because it managed to best diffuse the products made from them into its economy. In 1870, Germany’s economy was larger than the U.S’s by a third. By the outbreak of World War I, the American economy was two and a half times that of Germany. American industrial output exceeded the combined production of Germany and Britain. It’s true that none of those countries was the U.S.’s main geopolitical adversary, as China currently is. That’s why I argued that the U.S. and its allies should build a cushion of capacity to produce LFP and process battery metals and components. Almost no country produces 100% of its needs—everyone imports something. But you don’t want to rely on a single source for your entire supply of something critical. This history suggests that from a geopolitical and national economic standpoint, Ford was right to embrace CATL’s batteries. U.S. researchers invented LFP, today’s dominant type of lithium-ion battery. But CATL and China’s BYD were the ones to improve on it and scale it up. Their LFP is widely regarded as clearly superior to competing new LFP batteries produced by South Korea’s companies and others, and combined they sell more than half of all lithium-ion batteries in the world. Ford and Tesla have embraced China’s lead. In 2023—the year after its initial supply deal with CATL—Ford agreed to license CATL’s LFP technology, bringing in CATL engineers to help set up the equipment and show Ford employees how to use it. Ford has said it will fully operate the plant and a second in Kentucky where it also plans to make the batteries using CATL’s know-how. In 2024, Tesla acquired LFP production equipment from CATL, and in the first quarter this year it began using it for commercial production of cells at its Nevada factory. It’s not clear why, but Tesla has not drawn the same political fire as Ford has for working with the Chinese battery giant. What the two companies are doing aligns with the historical examples of U.S. companies embracing technology made by rivals abroad, mastering how to use it and spreading it into the economy. It’s also the playbook China followed in the 1990s. China invited foreign carmakers into the country on the condition that they teach its automakers how to build cars. For Volkswagen, General Motors, Tesla and other major Western carmakers, China for many years became one of their largest profit centers. Taking stock of those lessons, Chinese carmakers have now largely pushed out the foreigners and become the world’s largest exporter of cars. “Just like 20 years ago or whatever, China companies were using U.S. [intellectual property] to get companies up and running,” Truby said. “It’ll take a few years [for U.S. companies] to be able to develop the LFP batteries that are on level with CATL’s.” ---- Noteworthy Makers of flying electric taxis began their first flights under a federal program meant to get them into the air before they have obtained Federal Aviation Administration certification. Joby Aviation started demonstration flights in the Dallas area on Thursday and plans to pilot its flying taxi to 10 states over the coming months. Chinese electric carmaker XPeng launched automated production of its humanoid robot, Iron, in China. XPeng said it plans to make 1,000 of the robots per month by the end of the year, first introducing them into its own operations. Auto sales in China fell for the 11th straight month. According to official figures, car sales in the country fell 24% year on year in August. title: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Quietly Discussed an AI Safety Standards Body
content: Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have been holding discussions about working together to create a standards body for the AI industry, people familiar with the matter said, even before Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on Saturday for AI companies to coordinate on testing and auditing the technology. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, for his part, told staff at a companywide town hall meeting earlier this week that he supported a testing and auditing organization for the AI industry but believed that major AI labs would have to create a standards body on their own without the support of the U.S. government, a person familiar with the comments said. That kind of industry self-regulation was part of a broader proposal Amodei published on Saturday to slow AI development and establish independent oversight amid mounting risks posed by increasingly powerful AI. Amodei said companies could move ahead with voluntary safety standards while the government hammers out AI regulation, with the government potentially enabling or mediating industry discussions. Amodei’s post on X quickly garnered endorsements from several other tech leaders including Altman, who wrote that slowing cutting-edge AI development had been a topic of discussion at his company in recent weeks. Demis Hassabis, who recently stepped down as CEO of Google DeepMind, said the proposal was overall a step in the right direction, though some details “need working through.” SpaceX CEO Elon Musk also endorsed Amodei’s plan. The idea of a self-regulatory organization for AI has been part of the public conversation for several months. In July, Hassabis published an essay laying out a proposal for a self-regulatory body modeled after the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, which oversees U.S. broker-dealers and securities professionals. But the extent to which companies had already started working together on setting industry standards has not been previously reported. Since July, a working group of representatives below the CEO level from Google, Anthropic and OpenAI have been regularly meeting about the proposal for a standards body, according to people familiar with the matter. An executive order draft circulated in the White House that would have created such an organization, but the effort stalled in the late summer after failing to garner enough support within the Trump administration, The Information previously reported . Former White House AI czar David Sacks has been a vocal critic of creating a FINRA-like body for AI, arguing against involvement from the government. Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg also expressed his concerns about plans for a national AI regulator in an August phone call with President Donald Trump, Politico reported . In the town hall this week, Altman said that while he had been optimistic the government would support a standards body, there was not yet enough industry consensus, and some companies opposed the idea, the person familiar with the comments said. He added that the best path forward would be to try to do something with the other labs. Altman told employees at the same town hall that OpenAI could also slow its pace of development, Bloomberg reported . The working group meetings between Anthropic, OpenAI and Google about the industry-led standards body, which the people said are ongoing, signal appetite for action among the three labs beyond their executives’ high-profile public comments and proposals. The group met as recently as the past week, said one of the people. It’s unclear where Meta stands on the issue. On Saturday, Alexandr Wang, the company’s chief AI officer, wrote on X that “alignment is fundamental to delivering personal superintelligence for everyone,” referring to the idea of AI systems’ behavior adhering to the intent of the directions provided to them, though he did not specify support or opposition to Amodei’s proposal. Anthropic’s own employees drew fresh attention to concerns about the potential risks of increasingly powerful AI with posts that went viral on X in recent days. An Anthropic researcher said he was quitting the company because neither it nor OpenAI was “acting responsibly,” while a current Anthropic employee said the company genuinely believes AI could pose an existential threat to humanity. On Saturday, Amodei proposed that each leading AI company should give outside evaluators such as Model Evaluation and Threat Research the same access to their technology that employees receive, and he said that Anthropic was committing to the step. He also called on the government to enable AI companies to coordinate on safety without running afoul of antitrust laws, saying the government should issue a “narrow waiver” for certain conversations. Sacks said on X that AI companies should go ahead with the safety efforts and didn’t need an antitrust exemption to coordinate. But he questioned whether slowing development was “purely altruistic,” noting that product liability risks already provided a financial incentive to prevent AI from causing harm. Some in the AI industry were more critical of Amodei’s plan. Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez raised concerns in a post on X about the largest AI companies coordinating on rules that could constrain smaller rivals, writing, “Great ideas here from the cartel.”

title: The Download: AI’s real extinction threat and age-reversal tech for eyes
content:
The Download: AI’s real extinction threat and age-reversal tech for eyes
Plus: Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk have called for an AI slowdown.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Roundtables: could AI really kill us all?
Employees at the world's leading AI labs are saying there's a real possibility that advanced AI could destroy humanity. Are they right? Or is this more scaremongering and hype?
Join MIT Technology Review executive editor Niall Firth, senior AI editor Will Douglas Heaven, and AI reporter Grace Huckins for a subscriber-only conversation unpacking the debate around AI extinction. They’ll explore where the fears come from, whether they hold any water and, if they do, what we should do about them.
Register now to attend on Tuesday, September 15 at 16:00 BST / 11:00am EST / 8:00am PST.
Want to join the conversation? Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to all our Roundtables.
This geneticist’s age-reversal tech could help restore sight
Yuancheng (Ryan) Lu is obsessed with aging. And with eyes. As he steps outside the Whitehead Institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts, his aviator glasses darken automatically in the sun. Age-related blindness runs in his family, and his own 23andMe test came back with a mutation for macular degeneration, a top cause of vision loss in old age.
That obsession extends to his work. Lu is behind one of the coolest results in rejuvenation science and eye research: an age-reversal technique called reprogramming that repaired the optic nerves of blind mice, restoring their vision. Now, nearly the same genetic therapy he developed as a student has entered human clinical trials.
Learn more about Lu’s work on restoring sight with age-reversal therapy.
—Antonio Regalado
Yuancheng (Ryan) Lu is one of the biotechnology and health honorees on our 35 Innovators Under 35 list for 2026. Meet the rest of them here, or explore the full list across the biotechnology and health, AI, computing and robotics, and climate and energy categories.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk have called for an AI slowdown
In a rare show of unity, the rivals agreed that AI needs stronger brakes. (Guardian)
+ Amodei wants independent monitors and new industry-wide rules. (BBC)
+ Altman called for pacing, but not stopping. (Bloomberg $)
+ While Musk said on X that “Dario is right.”(WSJ $)
+ AI-linked stocks slumped in response. (FT $)
+ Chinese state media blasted the calls as a “Cold War” tactic. (Reuters $)
+ AI’s impacts are getting harder to predict. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Trump and Congress are resisting calls for stronger AI regulation
Trump downplayed AI risks, prioritizing the AI race with China. (NPR)
+ While the House Speaker said Congress won’t lead on AI regulation. (Politico $)
+ But Democrats are pushing for new rules before the midterms. (CNBC)
+ States and the White House are dividing over AI. (MIT Technology Review)
3 China plans to lead AI development across the BRICS countries
President Xi proposed open-source AI cooperation. (CNBC)
+ Beijing’s spy agency has warned of AI threats to national security. (FT $)
4 South Korea has tightened espionage laws to protect its chip secrets
Foreign spies can now face up to 30 years in prison. (FT $)
+ The changes follow alleged transfers of Samsung tech to China. (Reuters $)
5 The US and Mexico are teaming up to zap drones at the border
The operation may employ high-energy lasers.(Wired $)
+ Ukraine is a Wild West market for drone data. (MIT Technology Review)
6 AI agents are creating a new problem for the criminal justice system
The law has no clear answer when AI agents act independently. (Bloomberg $)
+ While courts face a flood of AI-generated lawsuits. (MIT Technology Review)
7 A Waymo pulled over and alerted police after detecting a gun
The riders were juveniles carrying a loaded AR-style ghost gun. (LA Times $)

title: Der Maschinenbau muss schneller werden – auch bei Textilien
content:
Der Maschinenbau muss schneller werden – auch bei Textilien
Rund 100 Experten aus Forschung und Industrie diskutierten bei der 18. Narrow Textile Conference (NTC) in Hof über neue Technologien für schmale Textilien – und über die Frage, wie schnell Forschung und Maschinenbau auf eine sich verändernde Welt reagieren müssen.
Es sind schmale Bänder, Geflechte und textile Strukturen, die bei der Narrow Textile Conference im Mittelpunkt stehen. Doch die Fragen, die dahinterstehen, sind groß: Wie lassen sich textile Produkte intelligenter machen? Welche neuen Materialien und Fertigungsverfahren werden gebraucht? Und wie kann eine Industrie, die stark von Maschinenbau und internationaler Produktion geprägt ist, mit dem Tempo des technologischen Wandels Schritt halten?
Rund 100 Teilnehmer aus etwa 40 Unternehmen, Forschungseinrichtungen und Organisationen kamen zur 18. Ausgabe der Konferenz. Den Auftakt bildeten am 31. August eine Führung durch die technischen Einrichtungen des Instituts für Materialwissenschaften in Münchberg und ein anschließendes Get-together, bevor die Konferenz am 1. und 2. September in Hof stattfand. Rund zehn Prozent der Gäste reisten aus dem Ausland an, unter anderem aus den USA, der Schweiz, Österreich, Frankreich und dem Iran. Die Konferenzsprache war Englisch.
Erstmals war die Hochschule Hof Gastgeber der Veranstaltung, die als Wanderkonferenz alle zwei Jahre an einem anderen Standort stattfindet. „Wir freuen uns über die große internationale Beteiligung und die Vielfalt der Fachbesucherinnen und Fachbesucher bei der Narrow Textile Conference. Besonders erfreulich ist, dass wir die Teilnehmerzahl verdoppeln konnten. Die erfolgreiche Ausrichtung der Tagung ist für uns zugleich eine große Anerkennung und Wertschätzung unserer Forschungsarbeit im Bereich der Schmaltextilien“, sagt Prof. Frank Ficker.
NTC startete in der Schweiz und tourt seitdem
Ihre Geschichte reicht bis ins Jahr 2001 zurück. Die erste Konferenz wurde anlässlich der Eröffnung des Jakob Müller Institute of Narrow Fabrics in Frick, Schweiz, veranstaltet. Nach weiteren Ausgaben bei der Jakob Müller Group in Frick folgten wechselnde Stationen an der Hochschule Niederrhein in Mönchengladbach und an der TU Dresden. Organisiert wurde die diesjährige Ausgabe vom Institut für Materialwissenschaften (ifm) der Hochschule Hof gemeinsam mit der Hochschule Niederrhein, der TU Dresden und der Jakob Müller Group.
Dass die Konferenz nach einer Pause wieder größer werden sollte, war dabei durchaus beabsichtigt. „Frischer Wind, ein neuer Name und deutlich mehr Teilnehmer als bei der letzten Tagung“ – so beschreibt Romy Ottiger, Organisatorin von der Hochschule Hof, die neue Ausgabe. Ein wissenschaftlicher Beirat der beteiligten Partner hatte dazu beigetragen, die Konferenz weiterzuentwickeln, darunter die Hochschule Niederrhein, die TU Dresden, die Jakob Müller Group und die Hochschule Hof.
Führung durch den Münchberger Textilstandort
Zum Auftakt erhielten die Teilnehmer am Münchberger Hochschulstandort Einblicke in die Forschung vor Ort. In den Maschinenhallen und technischen Einrichtungen konnten sie unter anderem Flechtmaschinen und 3D-Webmaschinen in Betrieb sehen. Damit blieb es nicht bei Vorträgen über neue Technologien: Die Besucher konnten sich unmittelbar davon überzeugen, woran in der Region geforscht und entwickelt wird. Am zweiten Tag verlagerte sich der Schwerpunkt nach Hof. Professor Frank Ficker, wissenschaftlicher Leiter des Instituts für Materialwissenschaften (ifm), stellte die Hochschule Hof und das ifm vor, bevor Dr. Janpeter Horn vom Verband Deutscher Maschinen- und Anlagenbau (VDMA) mit seiner Keynote den Blick über die Textilbranche hinaus auf die Entwicklung des Maschinenbaus richtete. Seine Botschaft war deutlich: „Die Welt ändert sich schneller als gedacht.“ Besonders die Dynamik der großen Wirtschaftsräume China und USA zwinge die deutsche und europäische Industrie dazu, sich schneller anzupassen. Wenn Produktion verlagert werde, folgten häufig auch die Investitionen, warnte Horn. Für einen Industriestandort wie Deutschland sei das problematisch.
Eine weitere Forderung richtete er an die Unternehmen und die Forschung: Innovation müsse schneller werden. Sie müsse nicht immer perfekt sein. Gerade Deutschland sei stark darin, bestehende Produkte zu optimieren. Die entscheidende Frage sei aber, ob es auch gelinge, wirklich neue Produkte und Märkte zu entwickeln.
Damit berührte Horn einen Punkt, der auch für die Hochschule Hof relevant ist: die enge Verbindung von Forschung und Industrie. „Als Institut an einer Hochschule haben wir eine starke Industrieprägung aufgebaut und konnten langfristige und erfolgreiche Partnerschaften mit der Industrie entwickeln. Für Unternehmen versuchen wir stets, neue Wege zu finden und zu ermöglichen“, so Ficker.
Zwischen Forschung und Industrie
Genau an dieser Schnittstelle bewegte sich die Konferenz: zwischen Materialforschung, Maschinentechnik und konkreten industriellen Anwendungen. Vorgestellt und diskutiert wurden Entwicklungen aus den vergangenen zwei Jahren, neue Projekte und technologische Ansätze für Schmalweberei, Flechttechnik und funktionale beziehungsweise intelligente Textilien. Eine Posterausstellung ergänzte die Fachvorträge und bot insbesondere jüngeren Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftlern eine Möglichkeit, ihre Arbeiten zu präsentieren. In einer begleitenden Fachausstellung präsentierten Unternehmen und Forschungseinrichtungen an Informationsständen ihre Technologien, Produkte und aktuellen Entwicklungen.
Der Wert der Veranstaltung liegt dabei nicht allein in einzelnen Forschungsergebnissen. Die Konferenz bringt Akteure zusammen, die sonst häufig in unterschiedlichen Welten arbeiten: Maschinenbauer treffen auf Materialforscher, Hochschulen auf Unternehmen, Entwickler auf Anwender. Daraus können neue Projekte, Produkte und Kooperationen entstehen.
Die nächste Ausgabe der Narrow Textile Conference ist für das erste Quartal 2028 in der Schweiz bei der Jakob Müller Group geplant.

Neue Mitgliedschaft verbindet langfristige Cybersicherheitsforschung mit digitaler Aufklärung, Vernetzung und gesellschaftlicher Resilienz.
Die Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit GmbH (Cyberagentur) ist neues Mitglied von Deutschland sicher im Netz e.V. (DsiN). Die Cyberagentur bringt künftig ihre Expertise zu neuen Technologien und langfristigen Cyberbedrohungen in das Netzwerk ein. Zugleich erweitert sie ihren Austausch mit Akteuren, die sich für Sicherheit und Kompetenz im digitalen Raum einsetzen.
Deutschland sicher im Netz engagiert sich seit 2006 für Cybersicherheit und digitale Kompetenz. Im Mittelpunkt stehen Bürgerinnen und Bürger sowie Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher sowie die Frage, wie sie digitale Angebote sicher, kompetent und selbstbestimmt nutzen können. Unter der Schirmherrschaft des Bundesministeriums des Innern vermittelt der Verein praxisnah Wissen zu digitalen Chancen und Risiken. Dafür bringt DsiN Akteure aus Zivilgesellschaft, Wirtschaft und Politik zusammen. Zu den Fokusthemen 2026 gehören digitale Identitäten, Künstliche Intelligenz, digitale Souveränität und Desinformation.
„Wer Cybersicherheit stärken will, muss heute schon an die Bedrohungen und Technologien von morgen denken“, erklärt Isabelle Rosière, Geschäftsführerin von Deutschland sicher im Netz e.V., „Mit der Cyberagentur gewinnt ‚Deutschland sicher im Netz‘ einen starken Partner, der Forschung, Innovation und digitale Souveränität konsequent vorausdenkt. Gemeinsam wollen wir dazu beitragen, dass aus technologischem Fortschritt auch mehr Sicherheit und digitale Resilienz für unsere Gesellschaft entstehen.“
Für die Cyberagentur eröffnet die Mitgliedschaft zusätzliche Möglichkeiten, Erkenntnisse aus der strategisch ausgerichteten Cybersicherheitsforschung in den gesellschaftlichen und fachpolitischen Diskurs einzubringen. Das DsiN-Netzwerk bietet hierfür unter anderem Dialogformate, Veranstaltungen, Publikationen und die Beteiligung an ausgewählten Projekten.
„Cybersicherheit braucht Vernetzung und den frühzeitigen Blick auf neue Risiken“, beton der Forschungsdirektor der Cyberagentur Prof. Dr. Christian Hummert. „Wir wollen unsere Forschungsexpertise in die Diskussion darüber einbringen, wie das Internet auch angesichts neuer Technologien in Zukunft sicher bleiben kann. Gleichzeitig bietet uns DsiN die Möglichkeit, gemeinsam mit unterschiedlichen gesellschaftlichen Akteuren für kommende Bedrohungen zu sensibilisieren. Forschung und digitale Aufklärung können sich hier sehr wirkungsvoll ergänzen.“
Die Mitgliedschaft verbindet damit zwei unterschiedliche Perspektiven: Die Cyberagentur untersucht technologische Entwicklungen und Sicherheitsfragen mit einem langfristigen Zeithorizont. DsiN adressiert digitale Sicherheit und Kompetenz in Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft. Der gemeinsame Austausch soll dazu beitragen, neue Risiken früher zu erkennen und Erkenntnisse über technologische Veränderungen breiter zugänglich zu machen.

title: Forschungsinitiative R+I Factory in Cottbus in Betrieb genommen
content:
Forschungsinitiative R+I Factory in Cottbus in Betrieb genommen
Brandenburgs Wissenschaftsministerin Dr. Manja Schüle startet die Initiative für KI und Mikroelektronik. Das Bundesforschungsministerium fördert das Projekt mit 15 Millionen Euro aus dem Strukturstärkungsgesetz. Das erste Modul AI-DISCO erforscht eine Plattform für verteilte KI.
In Cottbus ist heute die Research and Innovation Factory AI & Microelectronics feierlich eröffnet worden, eine langfristig angelegte Struktur für Forschung an Künstlicher Intelligenz und Mikroelektronik. Den Anfang macht AI-DISCO, das erste bewilligte Modul, das seit Februar 2026 läuft. Sieben Partner aus Forschung und Industrie erforschen darin bis Anfang 2030 eine Plattform für energieeffiziente, verteilte KI-Verarbeitung. Das Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) fördert AI-DISCO mit 15 Millionen Euro aus dem Strukturstärkungsgesetz; die Federführung liegt beim IHP – Leibniz-Institut für innovative Mikroelektronik.
Die Bedeutung des Vorhabens für den Technologiestandort Deutschland ordnet die Bundesministerin für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt, Dorothee Bär, so ein:
„Hier in Cottbus entsteht ein Vorbild für moderne Technologiepolitik. Die Research and Innovation Factory wird langfristig Kompetenzen in Künstlicher Intelligenz und Mikroelektronik aufbauen – von Industrie 4.0 bis zur Medizin – und damit einen wichtigen Beitrag zur technologischen Souveränität Deutschlands und Europas leisten. Mit ihrem ersten Modul AI-DISCO forscht die Initiative an Möglichkeiten, KI über dezentrale miteinander vernetzte Knotenpunkte zu nutzen statt an Großrechnern. Das ist technologische Zukunft und Strukturentwicklung in einem: Die Förderung stärkt die Lausitz als Innovationsstandort und schafft gleichzeitig strategische Fähigkeiten für den deutschen Industriestandort. Unsere Hightech Agenda Deutschland wird in Beispielen wie diesen konkret. Durch eigene, energieeffiziente KI-Chip-Entwicklungen wollen wir Deutschlands Position als Chip-Produktionsstandort Nr. 1 festigen."
Brandenburgs Ministerin für Wissenschaft, Forschung und Kultur, Dr. Manja Schüle, eröffnete die Initiative gemeinsam mit Prof. Dr.-Ing. Gerhard Kahmen, Wissenschaftlich-Technischer Geschäftsführer des IHP. Für das Land verbindet sich damit ein Beitrag zum Strukturwandel in der Lausitz:
„Mit AI-DISCO entsteht in Cottbus etwas, das weit über ein einzelnes Forschungsprojekt hinausgeht: Das Projekt will Künstliche Intelligenz und Mikroelektronik verbinden und Sensoren entwickeln, die selbst rechnen. Das macht industrielle Systeme schneller, energieeffizienter und unabhängiger von entfernten Rechenzentren. Besonders spannend finde ich, dass die Forscher dabei auf neuromorphes Rechnen setzen – also auf Chips, die sich am Vorbild unseres Gehirns orientieren. Wir setzen damit ganz bewusst auf Spitzenforschung und High-Tech als Motor des Strukturwandels in der Lausitz. Was hier aufgebaut wird, ist kein Trostpflaster für eine ehemalige Kohleregion. Sondern ein Standort, an dem die Technologien von morgen entwickelt werden – mit europäischem Anspruch. Wenn Sensoren künftig selbstständig denken können, dann sollte man wissen, wo sie es gelernt haben: in der Lausitz."
Was das für den Standort bedeutet, ordnet Prof. Dr.-Ing. Gerhard Kahmen, so ein:
„Mikroelektronik und Künstliche Intelligenz zusammenzubringen, eröffnet Anwendungen, die keine der beiden Disziplinen einzeln erreicht, in der Fertigung, in Edge-Cloud-Systemen, im Chipentwurf selbst. Dafür bündeln wir unsere Kompetenzen in der R+I Factory. Die R+I Factory ist mit ihrer inhaltlichen Ausrichtung ein wichtiger Beitrag zur weiteren Profilbildung und Sichtbarkeit des Forschungs- und Entwicklungsstandorts Cottbus."
Konkret erforschen die Partner Edge-Knoten, deren KI-Verarbeitung auf neuromorphen Schaltungen beruht und sich an Erkenntnissen der Neurobiologie orientiert. Dazu kommen Verfahren des föderierten Lernens, bei dem die Cloud die Knoten vortrainiert, statt alle Daten einzusammeln, sowie Fragen der Sicherheit und Ausfallsicherheit verteilter Systeme. Weil die Knoten häufig auf Batterie laufen, ist Energie dabei die knappste Größe.
Erprobt wird das an mehreren Anwendungsfeldern. In Energiesystemen soll räumlich verteilte Sensorik Abweichungen im Betrieb von Wind- und Solaranlagen früher erkennen, ohne dass alle Messdaten in ein Rechenzentrum wandern. Weitere Felder sind Industrie 4.0, Medizintechnik und Landwirtschaft, 6G-Kommunikation sowie Smart City und kritische Infrastruktur.
Welchen Nutzen die Industriepartner erwarten, macht ABB an der Automatisierungstechnik fest:
„In der Automatisierung fallen Entscheidungen in Bruchteilen von Sekunden. Wenn die Auswertung erst im Rechenzentrum stattfindet, kommt sie zu spät. Deshalb interessiert uns an AI-DISCO, dass die KI direkt in der Anlage rechnet." Dr. Martin Handreg, Automation Manager, ABB
Für den Standort Cottbus bedeutet die Initiative Zuwachs: Im Rahmen von AI-DISCO kommen mit dem Leibniz-Institut für Neurobiologie (LIN) und dem Deutschen Forschungszentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) zwei Forschungseinrichtungen neu hinzu. Die R+I Factory erweitert zugleich das Kooperationsnetzwerk am Lausitz Science Park und der Brandenburgischen Technischen Universität Cottbus-Senftenberg, deren Präsidentin Prof. Dr. Gesine Grande bei der Auftaktveranstaltung sprach.
Am Verbund beteiligt sind das IHP – Leibniz-Institut für innovative Mikroelektronik als Konsortialführer, die Brandenburgische Technische Universität Cottbus-Senftenberg, das DFKI – Deutsche Forschungszentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz, das Fraunhofer-Institut für Photonische Mikrosysteme IPMS, das LIN – Leibniz-Institut für Neurobiologie sowie die Unternehmen ABB und ENERTRAG.
Über die R+I Factory
Die Research and Innovation Factory AI & Microelectronics (R+I Factory) ist ein modular angelegtes Forschungs- und Innovationsvorhaben an der Schnittstelle von Künstlicher Intelligenz und Mikroelektronik in der Lausitz. Unter ihrem Dach bündeln Forschungseinrichtungen und Unternehmen ihre Arbeit an intelligenten Systemen und an der Hardware, auf der diese Systeme laufen; weitere Module werden schrittweise hinzukommen.
Über das IHP:
Das IHP – Leibniz-Institut für innovative Mikroelektronik in Frankfurt (Oder) forscht an siliziumbasierten Lösungen für die Mikro- und Nanoelektronik. Dabei verfolgt das IHP die gesamte Wertschöpfungskette von grundlegender Forschung bis zu anwendungsnahen Prototypen und Kleinserien. Forschungsschwerpunkte sind neue Materialien und Bauelemente, Halbleitertechnologien sowie Höchstfrequenz-Schaltungen und -Systeme für Anwendungsfelder wie Kommunikation, Industrie, Mobilität, Raumfahrt, Sicherheit und Medizin. Das Institut betreibt eine eigene Reinrauminfrastruktur unter industrienahen Bedingungen und bietet Kooperationspartnern aus Wissenschaft und Wirtschaft Zugang zu qualifizierten, weltweit führenden BiCMOS-Technologien. Das IHP ist Mitglied der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft und beschäftigt über 400 Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter. Es wird gemeinsam vom Bund und dem Land Brandenburg institutionell gefördert.

title: Korkia expands into offering 'powered land' for data centers in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Finnish company Korkia is expanding its investment strategy in Chile to include “powered land”, sites dedicated to data centers where land, permits, and grid access are already secured or in advanced stages. To meet the massive energy demands of these centers without straining the grid, Korkia plans to integrate these sites with new renewable energy generation and battery energy storage systems (BESS). Chile is one of four primary markets where Korkia is advancing these developments, alongside Finland, Sweden, and the UK. In Chile, Korkia already has projects that combine generation, storage, and new grid connection infrastructure. The Terrazas hybrid project, in the Coquimbo region, includes 280 MW of solar power and 1,240 MWh of storage. In April, the National Energy Commission authorized the 220 kV switching substation necessary for its connection to the National Electric System . At the beginning of September, Korkia also reported progress on two other Chilean projects: Mellizas, in Ñuble, which combines a 218 MW solar plant with an 800 MWh BESS and obtained environmental approval; and Beltrán, a 750 MWh independent storage system in the Valparaíso region that reached ready-to-build status . These assets are complemented by Paicaví, a 150 MW / 750 MWh BESS (Basic Substation Energy Saving System) planned for La Pintana, Metropolitan Region, which received environmental approval this year . The project involves an estimated investment of US$90 million and its connection to the grid near the Mariscal substation. Korkia maintains that its expertise in land acquisition, permitting, grid access, renewable generation, and storage will serve as the foundation for developing new data center sites. “Through our platform and local partnerships, we can bring together land, permitting, grid access, renewable generation, and energy storage,” Kantero noted. The company reports an advanced global portfolio of 15 GW comprising large-scale solar projects, wind power, BESS systems, and now also land designated for data centers. In addition, it maintains another 9 GW of renewable and storage projects in early stages of development. title: Engie and Return extend flexibility agreement for storage in Germany to 400 MW - Energy Storage
content: Engie and Return have expanded an existing agreement for the use of additional flexibility from battery storage facilities in Germany from 100 to 400 MW. The agreement is structured as a Virtual Flexibility Purchase Agreement (vFPA), the companies announced on Monday. Under this model, the agreement covers multiple battery storage facilities and does not pertain to a single plant. These facilities are bundled via the Virtual Flexibility Portfolio (VFP), and Engie then gains access to these battery storage facilities and their capacity through a single interface. Return and Engie signed the first vFPA of this kind in February for 100 MW of battery storage capacity. This was followed by another contract for 55 MW for installations in Spain. Engie and Return see potential in concluding similar agreements in other European countries as well. When the agreement was announced in February, the companies stated that it was a long-term (vFPA) with a fixed price . title: Inion Software launches VPP platform and white-label offer for batteries and renewable assets - Energy Storage
content: Lithuanian developer Inion Software has launched a virtual power plant (VPP) platform for storage and distributed energy assets. The company has dual aims: it is currently operational in Lithuania’s balancing market and expanding, while it also has a goal of rolling its VPP platform out as a white-label offering for energy companies and aggregators under their own brands. In Lithuania, Inion has currently connected 30 assets with a combined capacity of 160 MW, with the aim to aggregating the assets as a single portfolio across locations. The software also manages individual assets for charging, discharging, or adjusting output from solar or wind plants, helping them participate in the balancing market. In addition, the platform can also control multiple battery containers at the same site separately. Each container can have its own daily schedule and receive individual charging and discharging commands. Inion notes that the system can handle all balancing markets simultaneously across mFRR, aFRR, FCR, and day-ahead, intraday, and custom scenarios. It also said it uses “standard hardware at energy sites”, while its software connects the equipment to the platform and handles control. White-label option “We can offer the VPP as a white-label product,” said Šarūnas Stanaitis, CEO of Inion Software. “One of our strengths is integrating the hardware with the platform, which can be a difficult part of VPP deployment. Expanding this product outside Lithuania is one of our targets.” Cross-border expansion of European VPP software is often slowed by local regulations and fragmented TSO frameworks, limiting expansion prospects for companies that interact with grids. The company notes, as a white-label option, the architecture pairs standard hardware at the energy sites with Inion’s software to handle the equipment connection and control logic. title: Battery microgrid enables acaí processing in remote Amazon community - Energy Storage
content: A 50 kWp solar microgrid with 165 kWh of battery storage is replacing unreliable diesel generation at a remote community in Brazil’s Amazonas state, enabling local acaí processing and income generation. A solar-plus-storage microgrid is enabling a remote community in Brazil’s Amazonas state to start operating an açaí processing facility that had been planned for almost a decade. Installed in the Bela Conquista community in the Catuá-Ipixuna Extractive Reserve in Tefé, the system has 50 kWp of PV capacity and 165 kWh of battery storage. The initiative is part of the Luz na Floresta project, developed by the Sustainable Amazon Foundation (FAS), the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP) and Brazil’s Ministry of Mines and Energy (MME). The project aims to demonstrate how reliable electricity access can support economic activity in isolated Amazon communities. Before the microgrid was installed, the processing facility relied on diesel generation that was insufficient and intermittent. Power supply limitations contributed to production losses and restricted the volume of fruit that could be processed locally. The new infrastructure is expected to enable the facility to process up to 36,000 liters of açaí per year, allowing the community to add value to local production and increase household income. Daniel Gama, a Bela Conquista resident and president of the processing facility project, said unreliable electricity had been the main obstacle to starting operations. Problems with the existing distribution line meant the facility did not receive enough electricity to operate all its machinery. Luciana Sena, a community resident and deputy secretary of the açaí processing facility, said reliable electricity would reduce production losses and allow the facility to buy and process more locally produced fruit, increasing family incomes. In addition to the processing facility, the microgrid supplies electricity to essential community infrastructure, including a school, community center, community kitchen and water supply well. The project combines electrification with productive use of energy, a model that could be relevant in locations where conventional grid expansion presents logistical and economic challenges. The project also includes training residents to manage, operate and maintain the systems, with responsibility for the installed assets to be transferred to the communities. Thiago Carvalho, FAS renewable projects leader, said residents would receive training covering the management, operation and maintenance of the systems and would be responsible for those activities. The Global Energy Alliance said the initiative aims to demonstrate how electrification can support economic development while improving energy access. Luisa Valentim, the organization’s Brazil director, said it aims to use energy to create conditions for communities to remain in their territories while generating income and supporting Amazon forest conservation. Pilot projects Bela Conquista is the first practical demonstration of a model that the organizations plan to replicate through up to 20 pilot projects over the next two to three years, reaching as many as 25 communities in the Brazilian Amazon. Planned applications include bioeconomy activities such as açaí production and processing, fishing, agriculture and fruit processing. The program estimates that the solar-plus-storage systems could generate up to 1 GWh of solar electricity annually, avoiding the consumption of approximately 255,000 liters of diesel and 680 metric tons of CO2 emissions. The initiative aims to benefit more than 600 families while generating data and experience that could inform public policies for electrification and productive energy use in remote areas. The communities involved include the Serra da Moça Indigenous Territory in Boa Vista, Roraima; Nossa Senhora do Livramento (Uixi) in the Piagaçu-Purus Sustainable Development Reserve in Beruri, Amazonas; Bela Conquista in Tefé; the Tamaniquá community in the Middle Solimões region; and Santa Maria do Boiaçu, Cachoeirinha and Caicubi in the Lower Rio Branco region of Roraima. In the communities served, the project aims to achieve 80% energy availability and more than triple revenue from acaí production. For Bela Conquista residents, reliable electricity could also expand economic activities based on products already available in the forest, reducing the need to clear land for agriculture or livestock. Community leader Luzia Pinto said the community hopes to reduce deforestation for planting and livestock while becoming more reliant on extractive activities that make use of existing forest resources. The model is particularly relevant to the challenge of expanding electricity access across the Amazon, where long distances, dispersed populations and difficult terrain make conventional infrastructure expansion challenging. The Bela Conquista project places productive energy use at the center of the initiative. In addition to providing electricity, solar-plus-storage systems can enable communities to use that power for activities that generate local income. FAS General Superintendent Virgilio Viana said Bela Conquista demonstrates that the model can be replicated and that the main challenge is to multiply similar projects. title: U.S. government finalizes trade duties on solar imports from India, Indonesia, and Laos - pv magazine Global
content:
The U.S. Department of Commerce has issued final affirmative determinations in its antidumping and countervailing duty investigations targeting crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells and modules imported from India, Indonesia, and Laos.
Commerce reported a finding that manufacturers in all three nations dumped solar components into the U.S. market below fair value and benefited from government subsidies, resulting in material injury to the domestic solar manufacturing sector. The decision marks the conclusion of the Department of Commerce phase of the Solar IV trade litigation, originally brought by the Alliance for American Solar Manufacturing and Trade. Find an International Trade Administration
fact sheet here
In its final determination, Commerce established steep dumping margins and countervailing subsidy rates across mandatory respondents and all other producers in the targeted nations.
For Indian suppliers, Commerce calculated final dumping margins at 123.04% for all producers, alongside a countervailing duty rate set at 126.09%. Indonesian exporters face finalized dumping margins at 94.36% for all producers, with final countervailing duty rates ranging between 73.2% and 173.7%, depending on the specific manufacturer. For imports originating in Laos, Commerce set final dumping margins at 65.43% for all exporters, accompanied by countervailing subsidy rates established between 82.03% and 153.67%.
Unlike broader statutory actions like reciprocal tariffs or Section 232 national security measures, the trade measures are case-specific orders under the Tariff Act of 1930. The final antidumping and countervailing duties will stack directly on top of existing executive tariffs rather than replacing them.
The cases were initiated following petitions from the Alliance for American Solar Manufacturing and Trade, a coalition represented by lead petitioners First Solar, Hanwha Qcells USA, and Mission Solar Energy.
“America’s solar manufacturing sector is poised for a historic resurgence, with domestic module capacity up more than 750% since 2022 and cell production expanding as well,” said Tim Brightbill, co-chair of Wiley’s International Trade Practice and lead counsel to the Alliance. “But that progress is being harmed by dumped and subsidized imports from India, Indonesia, and Laos that have denied American producers a level playing field. Today’s final determinations are an essential step toward enforcing our trade laws and restoring fair competition for U.S. solar manufacturers and the workers they employ.”
Market context
While the Solar IV cases conclude, the market reality on the ground has already shifted. Cell procurement for U.S. module assembly has largely
migrated away from the target nations
, with primary cell volumes now originating in South Korea, the Philippines, and emerging African manufacturing hubs including Kenya, Nigeria, and Ethiopia. Meanwhile, South Korean cell suppliers face their own trade headwinds following a separate trade petition filed by the coalition American Manufacturers for Energy Resilience.
These finalized duties also arrive alongside structural administrative changes reshaping solar procurement. Federal trade rules recently
established Section 232 minimum import price floors
across the supply chain, setting statutory minimum entry prices of $21 per kilogram for raw polysilicon, $100 per kilogram for ingots and wafers, $0.22 per watt for solar cells, and $0.38 per watt for modules.
With government-mandated price floors governing imported components, industry observers note that the legal foundation for future antidumping and countervailing duty cases may lessen significantly. Because minimum import prices administratively dictate the baseline cost of foreign solar goods, proving that domestic manufacturers suffer material injury from unfair undercutting or dumped pricing becomes substantially harder to substantiate under U.S. trade law standards.
Next steps
The determination follows the U.S. International Trade Commission final hearing held earlier this week. The proceedings now turn to the Commission for its final injury vote, scheduled for October 14, 2026, to determine whether dumped and subsidized imports from the three nations materially injure or threaten the U.S. solar manufacturing industry.
If the International Trade Commission vote is affirmative, Commerce will issue official duty orders on November 2, 2026, imposing the finalized cash deposit rates. If the panel finds no material injury, the proceedings will terminate and all cash deposits previously collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection will be refunded.
The Solar IV cases follow the implementation of Solar III duty orders in June 2025 targeting imports from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam, which saw shipments from those four nations fall from $12.2 billion in 2023 to $1.3 billion in 2025.

title: Uniper’s Wilhelmshaven import terminal to progress after successful “Open Season”
content:
Uniper’s Wilhelmshaven import terminal to progress after successful “Open Season”
Enough reserve capacity to proceed with new terminal
Uniper has successfully completed “Open Season” for its future ammonia import terminal in Wilhelmshaven, Germany. The commodity giant reports that stakeholders have requested that enough future import capacity be reserved to advance the Wilhelmshaven project onto development, permitting and commercialization steps. Formal heads of term agreements and terminal use agreements with the successful “Open Season” participants will follow.
The Wilhelmshaven project itself comprises an ammonia-as-hydrogen import terminal (maximum annual throughput of 2.6 million tons of ammonia), an ammonia cracker (to be deployed in partnership with thyssenkrupp Uhde), 1 GW installed electrolysis to produce hydrogen, a hydrogen pipeline connection and a tie-in point to the future European Hydrogen Backbone, plus proximal access to future hydrogen off-takers in Lower-Saxony, North Rhine Westphalia and other German industrial clusters. Featuring a “modular design”, import capacity at the terminal can be scaled up to meet future demand, and Uniper indicates that it may launch additional “Open Seasons” in the future. Ammonia imports via Wilhelmshaven port could provide about 10-20% of Germany’s hydrogen demand in 2030.
As for the origin of the ammonia, in January 2026 Uniper and AM Green announced the signing of a long-term binding offtake agreement for renewable ammonia produced at AM Green’s under-development facility in Kakinada, on India’s east coast. 500,000 tons per year of RFNBO-certified ammonia will be shipped to Europe as early as 2028. Uniper is exploring low-carbon ammonia offtake in a variety of other global locations.
Learn more in Houston
Joining our opening keynote session at the upcoming Houston event is Benedikt Messner, Uniper Global Commodities’ Senior Vice President in Global Origination & LNG. You can hear directly from Benedikt and other “demand-makers” for ammonia energy (offtakers, consumers, mid-streamers, and traders of low-carbon ammonia) about their vision for future demand scenarios, as well as practical outcomes and recent progress. Don’t miss this high-profile discussion about the evolution of ammonia energy markets – from the all-important demand-side perspective.

title: Wolfram to replace grey hydrogen with green supply | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
Under a long-term agreement with regional utility Energie Steiermark, Wolfram will become a key customer for a new proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis plant in Bergla, around one kilometer from its St. Martin im Sulmtal site in Styria.
The facility will produce up to 750 metric tons of green hydrogen annually. Hydrogen will be delivered to Wolfram through a direct underground pipeline, replacing grey hydrogen produced from methane.
Hydrogen is an essential chemical input in Wolfram’s production process. It is used as a reducing agent to remove oxygen from tungsten oxide and produce tungsten metal powder. Carbon-based reducing agents cannot be used at this stage because tungsten readily reacts with carbon to form tungsten carbide.
The switch therefore allows Wolfram to reduce the emissions associated with hydrogen supply without changing the underlying chemistry of its tungsten production process.
The near-site production model is also designed to support supply reliability. The new facility will include redundant electrolysis capacity, while the direct pipeline connection will reduce Wolfram’s dependence on hydrogen transport over longer distances.
Wolfram will retain its existing hydrogen recycling system, which cleans and reuses hydrogen to the required pressure and purity standards.
The project illustrates how renewable hydrogen can decarbonize established industrial processes where hydrogen is already required as a chemical feedstock. It also links dedicated renewable hydrogen production with long-term industrial demand and local infrastructure.

title: ITER组织副总干事罗德隆一行到访中国聚变能源有限公司调研指导
content:
ITER组织副总干事罗德隆一行到访中国聚变能源有限公司调研指导
9月11日，国际热核聚变实验堆(ITER)组织副总干事罗德隆一行莅临中国聚变能源有限公司(以下简称“中国聚变”)调研指导，深入了解中国聚变发展总体情况与重点任务实施进展。中国聚变总经理张立波陪同调研。
调研期间，双方召开专题座谈会。张立波代表中国聚变对罗德隆一行的到访表示热烈欢迎，并对ITER组织及罗德隆先生对中国聚变的发展和ITER计划相关任务履约工作的关心、支持与指导表示衷心感谢。会上，中国聚变总工程师钟武律作总体情况报告，重点介绍了中国聚变发展现状和未来展望。双方围绕聚变能源领域的国际合作、重点工程建设、核心技术攻关等议题展开深入交流。罗德隆对中国聚变成立一年多来的快速发展表示赞赏，对取得的阶段性成果给予充分肯定，并感谢中国聚变在ITER计划执行过程中所作出的重要贡献。
随后，罗德隆为100余名干部职工作题为《ITER计划执行进展与展望》的专题讲座，系统分享全球大科学工程在协作管理、关键技术攻坚等方面的宝贵经验。讲座内容深入浅出，有效拓宽了参会人员的国际视野，深化了对全球聚变能源发展格局的理解。
会后，罗德隆一行实地考察上海聚变科学研究中心一期工程及高温超导磁体研发部(上重厂)，深入项目建设一线，详细了解工程进度、设备制造及现场管理情况，并就生产研制与项目推进工作提出专业指导意见。
此次调研交流为中国聚变进一步深化与ITER组织的合作、提升重大科研工程管理能力搭建了重要平台。未来，中国聚变将持续加强国际交流合作，加速推进聚变能源研发与产业化进程，积极服务国家“双碳”战略，为推动全球清洁能源转型贡献中国智慧与中国力量。
ITER组织施工司电源部门负责人李金超，中国聚变领导于雪峰、胡勇、钟武律、何延庆，公司办公室、规划发展部、科技与数字化部、产业投资部、上海基地工程管理部、聚变工程设计所等相关部门和单位负责人参加调研活动。

title: 全国首台自主化核级应急柴油发电机组“核柴一号”顺利出厂
content:
全国首台自主化核级应急柴油发电机组“核柴一号”顺利出厂
近期，全国首台自主化核级应急柴油发电机组“核柴一号”出厂仪式在沪东重机中高速机制造基地成功举办。在惠州核电、工程公司、沪东重机三方协同攻坚下，机组圆满完成全部厂内研制、试验、验收工作，具备包装发运条件，标志着我国8MW级核电应急柴油发电机组自主化落地取得里程碑式突破。惠州核电党委委员、副总经理韩霜、工程公司设备与成套中心质量总监徐光来、沪东重机董事李攀峰出席出厂仪式。
应急柴油发电机组是中国广核集团“8+1”关键核心设备，是保障核电厂安全稳定运行的核心兜底装备。首台套“核柴一号”柴油发电机组将服务于太平岭核电二期子项备用应急柴油发电机组0LHW系统。作为首台自主化设备，项目存在无成熟运维、调试经验可借鉴，技术新、标准高、容错率低等挑战。为有效破解首台套研制难题、顺利完成现场安装调试及运维等各项工作，惠州核电、工程公司、沪东重机三方深耕项目攻坚重点，深化党建与生产经营深度融合，联合组建党员攻坚队，以党建引领攻坚克难、聚力攻坚。全面复盘项目研制全过程，固化首台套优良实践经验，统一后续质量管控、技术服务、问题闭环管理标准，为设备现场落地筑牢基础。
本次项目同步推进设备数字化交付工作，在传统纸质资料交付基础上，完整沉淀机组三维模型、设计文件、试验报告、运维规程等数字化资产，搭建设备全生命周期数字档案。依托数字化成果，将有效提升设备安装调试、故障溯源、备件管理的精细化水平，为设备后期运维数字化、智慧电厂建设打下坚实基础。
下一阶段，三方将持续保持高效联动，充分发挥党员攻坚先锋作用，闭环管控安装、调试各个环节，及时处置现场技术难题;依托数字化交付资料，优化现场调试与后期运维管理流程，全力以赴保障“核柴一号”柴油发电机组高质量投运，为太平岭核电安全稳定运行筑牢坚实的应急动力屏障。

title: 华龙一号2.0防腐体系升级，中远关西联手中广核攻坚核电国产化涂料
content:
华龙一号2.0防腐体系升级，中远关西联手中广核攻坚核电国产化涂料
2026年9月2日，中远关西金山工厂迎来了一场关系到中国核电防腐技术未来的重要交流。中远关西总经理唐欢在此接待了中广核采购中心主任余雯钰一行，随行还有中广核采购中心相关业务负责人。中远关西工业防腐涂料部副总经理陈锦峰主持工作，技术中心主任江涛以及核心技术、市场团队悉数参会。双方围绕华龙一号2.0版防腐产品的联合研发项目展开深入交流，共同探讨核电高端防腐涂料技术创新与产业化应用的新路径。这场看似寻常的企业考察，实则承载着中国核电产业链自主可控的深层命题。
作为国内核电特种防腐涂料国产化的标杆企业，中远关西在核电涂料领域深耕多年，积累了深厚的研发与应用实力。公司是国内少数能够全覆盖主流核电堆型的涂料供应商，拥有核电涂料自主知识产权，成功打破了国外技术垄断。依托专业的研发平台与多年工程积淀，中远关西已服务国内三大核电集团，落地数十台核电机组项目，市场口碑与实战经验都很雄厚。这些硬实力背后，是一条从技术引进到自主创新、从单项突破到系统覆盖的国产化进阶之路。
座谈交流中，双方立足核电工程高端防腐领域的发展需求，围绕华龙一号2.0机组防腐体系升级、新型涂料产品研发、性能指标优化、工程适配性及落地应用方案展开了细致研讨。2026年8月，作为我国最先进的核电技术，华龙一号2.0版已获国务院核准并启动示范工程建设。该技术是华龙一号的迭代升级版本，设计寿期延长至80年，安全性与经济性全面提升。这一重大工程节点，对防腐涂料提出了更为严苛的要求，包括更长的服役寿命、更强的环境适应性和更高的安全冗余。中远关西技术团队结合自身技术优势，详细阐述了专项研发思路与技术攻关方向，全力匹配华龙一号2.0升级迭代需求。从配方设计到性能验证，从实验室数据到工程场景模拟，每一项技术方案都指向一个目标：让国产防腐涂料在最高标准的核电工程中经得起时间与安全的双重检验。
中广核采购中心代表团充分肯定了中远关西的技术积淀与研发实力。结合项目建设标准与实际场景，代表团提出了优化需求，双方就研发进度、技术对接、落地合作模式达成初步共识。双方一致认为，本次联合研发对完善核电国产化防腐体系、提升核电工程安全保障能力意义深远。这种以需求牵引研发、以研发支撑工程的协同模式，正是中国核电产业链走向成熟的标志。
交流期间，余雯钰一行实地参观了中远关西技术中心研发实验室与检测平台，深入了解涂料配方研发、性能测试、质量管控全流程体系。从原材料筛选到成品出厂，从加速老化实验到极端工况模拟，每一个环节都直观展现了企业高端涂料研发的硬实力。参观过程中，双方技术人员的交流不断深入，从微观配方到宏观应用，从当前需求到未来迭代，诸多技术细节在对话中逐渐清晰。
此次交流进一步加深了双方的战略协同。中远关西将以核电涂料国产化为突破口，勇担核心技术自主可控的使命，加速创新成果的转化，以极致品质筑牢核电安全基石。双方携手共进，将有力推动民族产业链升级，为"双碳"目标下核电强国建设贡献硬核力量，共同塑造中国智造的新标杆。
从一座工厂的实验室到数十台核电机组的工程现场，从一项技术突破到整个产业链的协同，中远关西与中广核的这次握手，不仅是一次商业合作的推进，更是中国核电防腐技术从跟跑到领跑的生动注脚。当华龙一号2.0在未来的示范工程中拔地而起，那些看不见的防腐涂层将成为守护核电安全的第一道防线，也是中国制造向中国创造跨越的无声见证。

title: 国家能源局党组书记、局长王宏志署名文章：加快建设新型能源体系 支撑能源强国建设
content:
国家能源局党组书记、局长王宏志署名文章：加快建设新型能源体系 支撑能源强国建设
能源保障和安全事关国计民生。习近平总书记指出：“加快规划建设新型能源体系，确保能源安全。”党的二十届四中全会《建议》和“十五五”规划纲要提出“建设能源强国”，为能源高质量发展提供了根本遵循和行动纲领。《新型能源体系建设“十五五”规划》细化落实了有关任务。“十五五”时期，要深入践行“四个革命、一个合作”(能源消费革命、能源供给革命、能源技术革命、能源体制革命和全方位加强国际合作)能源安全新战略，加快建设清洁低碳安全高效的新型能源体系，确保能源的饭碗牢牢端在自己手里。
充分认识新型能源体系建设的原则要求
当前，世界百年变局加速演进，全球能源格局深度调整，我国能源发展战略机遇和风险挑战并存。加快建设新型能源体系，是顺应能源发展大势的必然选择，是建设能源强国的关键路径。必须深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于能源安全的重要论述，把握以下原则要求。
坚持系统观念，推进能源绿色低碳转型。绿色低碳发展是经济社会发展全面转型的一项复杂工程和长期任务。习近平总书记强调：“我们要提高战略思维能力，把系统观念贯穿‘双碳’工作全过程”。当前，新能源安全可靠替代能力有待提升，化石能源面临转型降碳和兜底保障双重压力。“十五五”时期，必须处理好供给与消费、新能源与传统能源、当前与长远、全局与局部等关系，强化节能降碳导向，坚持风光水核等多能并举，先立后破促进能源绿色低碳转型。
坚持人民至上，实现发展成果共享。民生用能水平是衡量一个国家一个地区现代化程度的重要标准。习近平总书记强调：“要统筹做好重要民生商品保供稳价和煤电油气运保障供应”。当前，我国城乡区域能源发展尚不均衡，人民用能需求正在从“有没有”向“好不好”转变。“十五五”时期，必须深入践行能源为民的理念，发挥能源产业带动就业增收作用，全面提高能源服务保障水平，更好满足人民日益增长的美好生活用能需求。
坚持底线思维，强化能源安全保障。习近平总书记强调：“能源安全事关经济社会发展全局。”当前，国际局势纷繁复杂，我国能源发展面临需求压力巨大、供给制约较多、绿色低碳转型任务艰巨等一系列挑战。“十五五”时期，必须增强能源产供储销体系韧性，有效防范化解各类风险，以国内能源供应的确定性应对外部环境的不确定性。同时，坚持能源进口多元化，强化开放条件下的能源安全。
坚持创新驱动，增强能源发展动能。创新是引领能源发展的第一动力。党的二十届四中全会《建议》对能源科技、产业和体制机制创新作出系统部署。“十五五”时期，一方面，要聚焦能源关键领域和重大需求，推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合，因地制宜发展能源新质生产力，打造高水平自主可控的能源产业链。另一方面，要聚焦制约能源高质量发展的深层次问题，加强体制机制创新，促进能源要素市场化配置，鼓励新模式新业态发展，健全能源价格形成和传导机制，以改革办法破解发展难题。
准确把握“十五五”新型能源体系建设方向目标
“十五五”规划纲要明确“清洁低碳安全高效的新型能源体系初步建成”，这是今后5年能源工作的总体方向，具有丰富内涵。
安全韧性更足。能源是经济社会发展的重要基石。“十五五”时期，能源综合生产能力要达到58亿吨标准煤，国内油气供应量达到4.4亿吨油当量;全国电力总装机达到54亿千瓦，电力供应充裕度保持合理水平，电力系统互补互济和安全韧性水平全面提升;能源储备种类、规模和方式更加合理，进口保持多元可控，应急处置和风险管控更加有力有效。
能源结构更绿。能源是推进碳达峰碳中和的主战场。“十五五”时期，要推动风电和太阳能发电装机比重超过50%、成为电力装机主体，非化石能源发电量比重达到50%、成为电量主体，单位发电量碳排放下降10%以上，加快推进新增用电量由新增清洁能源电量覆盖，非化石能源消费比重达到25%。煤炭和石油消费达峰，支撑如期实现碳达峰目标。
系统形态更新。近年来，我国能源系统形态和运行方式不断创新。“十五五”时期，要初步建成新型电力系统，以及主配微协同的新型电网，电力需求响应能力达到最大用电负荷的5%以上，源储调节能力增长40%以上，智能电网和微电网加快建设，虚拟电厂、车网互动等新模式新业态广泛发展。电力、热力、氢能等多能互补发展，氢能和绿色燃料实现跨区域管输。能源与用能产业深度融合，电力与算力高度协同。
创新活力更强。改革创新是推动能源高质量发展的动力源泉。“十五五”时期，能源产业链关键技术装备要实现总体自主可控，新能源、新型储能、先进核电等战略性新兴产业集群化发展，氢能等未来能源产业战略布局初步形成，形成一批“人工智能+”能源典型应用场景。适应新型能源体系的市场和价格机制加快健全，基本建成全国统一电力市场体系，能源高质量发展活力显著增强。
扎实推进“十五五”规划落地见效
“十五五”时期，要锚定新型能源体系和能源强国建设战略目标，以规划实施为抓手，切实推动各项重大战略任务、重大改革举措和重大工程项目落实。
完善能源空间布局。高质量打造非化石能源增长高地，建设“三北”风电光伏基地、西南水风光一体化基地、沿海核电基地和海上风电基地，大力发展分布式能源。“十五五”时期，新增风电光伏发电装机10亿千瓦左右。夯实化石能源生产基础，优化建设山西、蒙西、蒙东、陕北、新疆五大煤炭供应保障基地，加强鄂尔多斯、塔里木、渤海湾等重点盆地和海域油气产能建设。推动能源开发与用能产业协同布局，统筹西电西用与西电东送，加强产业转移与清洁能源协同布局，促进算电协同发展。统筹优化能源骨干通道布局，推动西电东送能力达到4.2亿千瓦以上，持续优化西煤东运、北煤南运通道布局，加强油气“全国一张网”建设。拓展能源多元进口通道，巩固四大油气进口战略通道，巩固完善煤炭进口通道格局。
强化战略任务协同。聚焦端牢能源饭碗，构建坚强韧性的能源安全保障体系、立体多元的能源国际合作体系，统筹能源战略安全、转型安全和应急安全，夯实国内生产供应基础，提升能源多元保障能力。聚焦能源转型发展，构建先进适配的新型能源基础设施体系、绿色低碳的能源消费体系，实施非化石能源十年倍增行动，以新型电网为重点加快构建新型电力系统;同时，更大力度推进重点领域节能降碳，深入实施清洁能源替代，推动热力系统绿色低碳转型。聚焦能源改革创新，构建自立自强的能源科技创新体系、协同高效的现代化能源治理体系，统筹推进能源传统产业、新兴产业和未来产业创新发展，促进人工智能与能源双向赋能;深化能源市场化改革，完善能源价格、投资、运行、监管等体制机制。
夯实工程项目支撑。工程项目是规划实施的重要抓手。一方面，实施一批重大战略工程。高质量建设雅下水电等重大工程，加快推进“沙戈荒”等新能源基地、水风光一体化基地、海上风电等基地建设，积极安全有序推进沿海核电项目建设。统筹推进新型电网重大工程建设，加大跨省区输电通道、省间互济工程、电网主网架和配电网等投资建设力度。完善油气“全国一张网”，加强干线管道及互联互通工程建设。另一方面，积极建设新产业新业态项目。实施电动汽车充电网络提升工程，布局建设风光氢氨醇一体化基地，建设光热发电工程，加快推进绿电直连和智能微电网发展，建成一批零碳园区。预计“十五五”能源重点项目和新业态投资超过20万亿元。
健全规划实施机制。在国家能源委员会统筹指导下，压实目标任务实施主体责任，明确时间表和路线图，加强跨领域跨部门跨地区协调对接。强化规划实施政策协同，制定支撑规划目标任务的政策文件，加强项目建设要素保障，落实促进能源绿色低碳发展的财税、金融、投资、价格、科技、环保等政策。完善规划实施工作机制，加强能源发展形势分析和监测评估，做好年度计划与规划实施衔接，确保规划落地见效。

content:
美国联邦聚变系统公司获韩国现代10亿美元投资
近日，由比尔·盖茨支持的美国核聚变公司Commonwealth Fusion Systems已获得韩国现代汽车集团10亿美元投资，用于建设其商业聚变电站。
现代汽车集团执行副总裁郑浩恩表示，该计划将使双方能够探索在名为ARC的商业聚变电站项目上的工程合作。聚变能源有望在满足日益增长的全球能源需求方面发挥重要作用，同时支持更可持续的未来。
截至今年六月，这套硬件方案在物理可行性方面已获得正式的学术确认。在一项经过同行评审的研究之后，CFS验证了ARC设计中关于核心聚变物理的种种假设，其相关模型也显示，ARC电站将产生约11亿瓦的聚变功率，进而向电网输送约4亿瓦的净电力。

title: 韩国庆州议会深入考察月城核电站及放射性废物处理设施
content:
韩国庆州议会深入考察月城核电站及放射性废物处理设施
近日，韩国庆州议会组织了一次深入的实地考察，此次考察的重点是月城核电站和韩国原子能环境公团。考察团旨在对核电站的运营安全和放射性废物处理设施的运作进行全面了解，并听取相关人员的意见反馈。
此次行动的出发点，是为了深入调查与市民安全息息相关的核心议题，包括核电站的安全管理状况和放射性废弃物处理设施的运营模式。议员们希望透过这次考察，能更直观地了解实际情况，并为制定更完善的政策提供参考。
在考察的开始阶段，议员们前往月城核电站，听取了关于核电站运营情况的详细介绍。随后，他们重点参观了使用后核燃料干式储存设施“Maxter”，仔细检查了储存设施的运营细节和管理状态，以确保其安全可靠。
为了更全面地了解核电站的运作情况，考察团还前往月城3号核电站，就核电站的日常运营以及使用后核燃料湿式储存设施的管理情况进行了深入调查。现场人员就操作流程、安全措施等方面进行了详细说明。
随后，考察团又转移到韩国原子能环境公团，继续深入了解中低放射性废弃物的管理现状。议员们认真听取了相关负责人的报告，并就相关问题进行了深入的提问和讨论，力求对废物处理的各个环节都有清晰的认识。
为了更直观地了解处理过程，议员们还参观了第二阶段表层处置设施的观景台，考察了设施的设置和运作，对整个放射性废弃物的处理流程有了更为具体的印象。
在考察过程中，议员们一致强调，确保核电站和放射性废物相关设施的安全稳定运行和严格管理是首要任务。他们认为，这关系到公众的安全和福祉，必须得到高度重视。
与此相关，议员们还向相关部门提出，要与当地居民保持持续的沟通，并公开相关信息，以增强公众的信任和理解。同时，他们还呼吁建立更完善的安全体系，为市民营造一个安心的生活环境。
通过此次实地考察，庆州议会希望能够更加深入地了解核电安全和废物处理方面的实际情况，并为保障市民的健康和安全贡献自己的力量。
庆州市议会(通常简称庆州议会)是韩国庆尚北道庆州市的基层地方议会和立法机构，负责审议和决定庆州市的条例、预算及地方行政事务。

title: 俄罗斯第二座贫铀六氟化物加工厂正式投产 铀转化产能有望翻倍
content:
俄罗斯第二座贫铀六氟化物加工厂正式投产 铀转化产能有望翻倍
位于克拉斯诺亚尔斯克边疆区泽列诺戈尔斯克电化学厂的贫铀后处理设施，已于近日正式启用。据俄罗斯国家原子能公司总经理阿列克谢·利哈乔夫发表声明确认，这一新设施的投运，使俄罗斯在贫铀六氟化物(DUHF)后处理方面的能力实现翻番。这也是俄罗斯建成的第二座此类DUHF加工厂，其年产能达到1万吨，而此前同厂内运营的第一座同类工厂已在此先行投产。
利哈乔夫在声明中表示，新建贫铀六氟化物后处理设施的投产，对于电化学工厂、俄罗斯国家原子能公司燃料部门以及整个俄罗斯核工业而言，都堪称意义重大的事件。他所称的这项技术，将有助于把俄罗斯的贫铀转化能力提升一倍，即达到每年2万吨的水平，同时确保把贫铀转化为化学安全的形态，从而得以安全储存，不会对生态环境构成任何风险。
随着第四代核技术的不断发展，利哈乔夫进一步指出，贫铀已不再是废料，而是面向未来的能源战略资源。这一判断，反映出俄罗斯核工业在资源利用与循环利用方面正在发生的深刻转变，贫铀的正当作用正被重新审视和开发。
俄罗斯国家原子能公司燃料部门的管理公司TVEL总裁娜塔莉亚·尼基佩洛娃，在该设施的启动仪式上宣布，经脱氟工艺获取的贫铀将被用于生产核反应堆的混合氧化物(MOX)以及混合氮氧化物(MNUP)燃料。她表示，鉴于全球需求持续增长、铀价高企，加之俄罗斯拥有新一代技术，任何铀，无论其铀-235同位素含量高低，对工业界都具有巨大的价值。
尼基佩洛娃强调，俄罗斯的离心机能够对贫铀六氟化物进行高效再浓缩，而其快堆技术则允许在核燃料中使用钚和贫铀等二次核材料。通过对贫铀六氟化物实施脱氟处理，俄罗斯不仅实现了铀的闭环回收，也实现了氟的闭环回收，回收的氟还可再次用于转化环节，从而形成完整的循环利用链条。
在这一加工过程中所产生的含氟产品，包括氢氟酸和无水氟化氢，也以认证化学品的身份在市场上出售。这些产品既供应给俄罗斯国家原子能公司的下属工厂，也面向化工、冶金和石油天然气等行业的相关公司，展现出多领域应用的市场潜力。
关于TVEL，作为俄罗斯国家原子能公司燃料事业部的管理公司，TVEL股份公司拥有核燃料制造、铀转化与浓缩、气体离心机生产以及研发机构等完整设施。作为俄罗斯核电站唯一的核燃料供应商，TVEL向多达15个国家的70余座动力反应堆、9个国家的研究反应堆以及俄罗斯核电站的运输反应堆持续供应燃料，成为全球每六座动力反应堆中就有一座选用其燃料的重要企业。

title: 韩国韩蔚核电站开展高强度综合演习 应对地震、野火及无人机等安全威胁
content:
韩国韩蔚核电站开展高强度综合演习 应对地震、野火及无人机等安全威胁
14日，韩国水力原子力（KHNP）韩蔚核电站开展了高强度的综合应急演练，旨在应对地震、山火、放射性物质泄漏等复合型灾害，以及信息系统瘫痪、无人机威胁等新型安全挑战。
韩蔚核电站宣布联合多个相关部门，在韩蔚1号机组正式举行了“2026年灾害应对安全韩国演习”
“安全韩国演习”是一项全国性的综合应急演练，旨在建立包括韩国中央各部委、地方政府及公共机构在内的灾害管理体系与跨部门协作机制，确保在重大突发事件中具备高效的联合处置能力。
本次演习被韩国行政安全部选定为今年下半年的试点演练项目。自6月起，韩蔚核电站便联合蔚珍郡政府、消防部门及警察局等机构多次召开筹备会议，并在引入民间专家咨询后完成了预演，为本次正式演练奠定了基础。
演习设定了极具针对性的高难度复合灾害场景：模拟韩蔚核电站附近海域发生地震，并接连引发山火、厂区火灾及放射性物质泄漏。此外，演习还特别融入了信息系统故障、非法无人机入侵等新型安全威胁，全方位检验核电站的极端应对能力。

韩国总统李在明会见亚洲开发银行总裁 拟扩大核矿、AI及核电领域合作
近日，韩国总统李在明会见了亚洲开发银行(ADB)总裁神田雅人，双方就深化合作达成多项共识。此次会晤以韩国与中亚地区领导人的外交互动为契机，双方提议结合韩国的技术实力与亚洲开发银行的金融手段，共同拓展在亚太地区的合作空间。
会晤当天，李在明总统在上午11时的办公室接见了神田总裁。此次访问正值神田出席韩乌首脑会谈及首次韩中亚首脑会议期间。青瓦台首席发言人姜有正在书面简报中表示，此次会面为韩亚两方在能源与科技领域的重要交流平台。
李在明首先指出，中亚地区凭借丰富的自然资源和优越的地理位置，具备巨大的增长潜力。他借此机会提出扩大韩国与亚洲开发银行之间合作的建议，希望将双方的优势结合起来，实现互利共赢。
在核心矿物供应链方面，李在明特别强调，为了确保以乌兹别克斯坦为代表的中亚地区核心矿物供应链的稳定，拥有丰富项目经验和金融实力的亚洲开发银行与韩国应加强合作。神田总裁则指出，核心矿物供应链正是亚洲开发银行重点支持的领域，他对与具备工业能力的韩国展开合作表达了积极意愿。
就人工智能领域，李在明介绍了韩国推动的"人人共享的AI"愿景，以及在全球AI发展中作出的努力。他强调，若能將韩国的AI能力与亚洲开发银行的开发专业性结合起来，必将在亚太地区取得显著成果。神田总裁评价称，尽管全球经济形势充满不确定性，韩国经济仍展现出卓越的表现，并对李在明在AI和数字领域所展现出的"惊人领导力"表示钦佩。
在能源基础设施方面，双方一致决定进一步扩大合作。李在明表示，双方将共同努力，确保韩国的技术和经验能够应用于亚洲开发银行正在推进的东盟电网等亚太能源基础设施扩展项目。同时，韩国将加大对核电领域的金融支持政策投入，为相关项目提供有力保障。
神田雅人总裁还对即将举行的韩国中业首脑会议表示祝福。他表示，双方期待此次会议能够取得圆满成功，并为韩亚两方在多领域合作的深化奠定坚实基础。作为首次韩中亚首脑会议的重要前奏，此次会晤被视为推动地区经济一体化和技术合作的重要一步。
此次会晤不仅为韩国企业拓展海外市场创造了新的机遇，也为亚太地区的能源转型和数字化发展注入了新的动力。双方在此框架下的深入合作，有望为整个亚太地区带来更为广泛的发展红利。

title: 韩国加强核电站周边无人机管控，非法飞行将触犯刑事法
content:
韩国加强核电站周边无人机管控，非法飞行将触犯刑事法
2026-09-14 18:00 韩国核电
韩国水力原子力公司(KHNP)于9月14日表示，将进一步加强对核电站周边禁飞区域内未经批准无人机飞行行为的应对。
据了解，根据修改后的《航空安全法》，在禁飞区内未经许可擅自操作超轻型飞行装置(无人机等)的处罚标准，已从原先的“300万韩元以下罚款(行政罚款)”大幅提高至“1年以下有期徒刑或1000万韩元以下罚金”。
据韩国原子能安全委员会统计，自2021年至去年8月，在韩国全国各核电站附近共探测到非法无人机699起，其中有284起未能确认操作人员的身份。

title: 俄罗斯国家原子能公司完成 BREST 反应堆堆芯空腔第一阶段混凝土浇筑
content:
俄罗斯国家原子能公司完成 BREST 反应堆堆芯空腔第一阶段混凝土浇筑
俄罗斯国家原子能公司(Rosatom)旗下 TVEL 燃料公司宣布，位于汤姆斯克州塞维尔斯克的未来创新核电机组“BREST-OD-300”顺利完成了反应堆堆芯内部空腔的第一阶段混凝土浇筑工作。
该反应堆坐落于西伯利亚化学综合体(SCC)区域内的第四代经验示范能源综合体(ODEK)场地，属于俄国家级战略行业项目“突破(Proryv)”的核心组成部分。消息指出，反应堆本体的混凝土浇筑将分多个阶段推进，预计于2027年冬季全部完工，届时使用的耐热混凝土总量将超过7000立方米。
BREST-OD-300 反应堆采用了一体化布局设计。与常见的 VVER 压水堆整体金属结构不同，该反应堆本体采用金属-混凝土复合结构，内部装配有用于容纳堆芯和一回路设备的金属空腔。这些空腔之间的空间将分阶段充填混凝土，使混凝土不仅作为承重结构的一部分，同时承担热防护与辐射防护的功能。
SCC 经验示范能源综合体(ODEK)总监德米特里·佐祖利亚表示：“这种反应堆本体设计在国际核电实践中尚无先例。BREST-OD-300 的一体化布局使其具备极高的内在安全性与可靠性。”
“突破”项目是俄罗斯国家原子能公司(Rosatom)的一项关键战略，它汇集了多种未来核技术，包括核燃料制造模块、配备创新型BREST-OD-300反应堆的发电单元以及乏燃料后处理模块。 这一综合体的建设，标志着全球首座集快堆和现场闭式核燃料循环于一体的核电站的诞生。
第四代核电系统(G4NPS)是国际原子能机构(IAEA)分类中的一种新型核电系统，它旨在通过技术创新，显著提升核能的安全性、拓展燃料选择范围并减少核废物的产生。俄罗斯作为G4NPS技术的领先开发者，正在积极推动相关技术的研发和应用。

title: 韩国核安全基金会与美国 IEEE 签署 MRA，提升核电设备性能验证国际可信度
content:
韩国核安全基金会与美国 IEEE 签署 MRA，提升核电设备性能验证国际可信度
韩国核安全基金会(理事长 金成真)于 14 日在京畿道城南市与美国电气与电子工程师协会(IEEE, The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Incorporated)正式签署了核电设备性能验证领域的相互认可协议(MRA, Mutual Recognition Agreement)。
本次 MRA 的核心在于：双方互相承认各自运行的性能验证认证体系具备同等水平的专业能力与质量管理能力。根据协议，韩国核安全基金会与 IEEE 将互相确认对方的性能验证体系持续保持同等水平。此外，通过两家机构审查与认证的性能验证机构，将获发印有韩国核安全基金会及 IEEE 标志以及 MRA 相关事项的联合认证证书。
核电设备性能验证是指确认安装在核电站内的安全相关设备，在遭遇地震、高温高压、强辐射等极限环境时，仍能正常执行所要求的安全功能的核心程序。该环节直接关系到核电站的安全性能，因此验证机构的专业能力、技术水平及质量保证体系的客观管理至关重要。
IEEE 作为制定电气与电子领域国际技术标准的专业机构，其标准被广泛应用于韩国内外核电设备的设计与性能验证中。特别是在美国，IEEE 针对部分核电设备性能验证机构运行着专门的认证制度，在核电设备验证领域拥有极高的国际影响力。
韩国核安全基金会理事长金成真表示，通过本次 MRA，原本局限于韩国国内的核电设备性能验证机构认证体系，得以与享誉国际的 IEEE 站在同一高度，这也是韩国迈向全球领先机构行列的重要协定。希望通过加强与 IEEE 的国际合作，进一步提升韩国内外开展的核电设备性能验证的可信度，并最终为提高核电安全性做出贡献。

title: Kairos Power在田纳西州组建先进核电制造与预制中心
content:
Kairos Power在田纳西州组建先进核电制造与预制中心
2026-09-14 14:09 美国核电
近期，凯洛斯能源公司(Kairos Power)在田纳西州橡树岭宣布发起一项名为"先进制造与预制核电中心"(简称NuCAMP)的倡议，旨在推动新型制造工艺与施工技术在核电领域走向成熟，同时为东田纳西州培养具备专业技能的产业工人。NuCAMP的核心目标是支撑先进核反应堆在未来大规模部署落地。
根据已签署的谅解备忘录，Kairos Power将牵头主导这一倡议，并与橡树岭国家实验室、田纳西大学诺克斯维尔分校、先进复合材料制造创新研究所(IACMI)、巴纳德建筑公司、罗恩州立社区学院、查塔努加州立社区学院以及橡树岭学校等多方机构展开协作。此外，凯洛斯动力还与国际合作伙伴三星C&T工程建筑集团和剑桥真空工程技术公司共同探索合作机会，为NuCAMP提供先进制造与施工领域的战略咨询服务。
这些合作机构一致同意进入为期12个月的初步探索阶段，以明确各方如何协同配合，一方面为核工业应用开发并验证先进制造与施工技术，另一方面为工程师和熟练技术工人构建通往实际应用领域的发展路径。凯洛斯动力首席技术官兼联合创始人埃德·布兰德福德表示，要实现先进反应堆的大规模低成本交付，仅凭出色的设计设计远远不够，还需要创新的制造工艺作为支撑、用于资质认证的代码依据，以及掌握相应技能的人才来实施建造工作。

title: 俄罗斯将增加伊朗布什尔(Bushehr)核电站的技术人员数量
content:
俄罗斯将增加伊朗布什尔(Bushehr)核电站的技术人员数量
俄罗斯国有核电企业俄罗斯原子能公司(Rosatom)即将显著增强其在伊朗布什尔核电站的技术力量。据报道，该公司计划在接下来的几个月内把派驻该设施的专业技术人员规模扩大到150名。
布什尔发电站是伊朗国家能源战略的重要组成部分，能够为区域电网提供电力。多年来，与俄罗斯原子能公司的合作对核电站的正常运转不可或缺，俄方面负责监督各项技术升级和安全评估工作。此次计划增派的人员，是在一段持续倚重俄罗斯核领域专家的时期之后作出的，目的在于确保该设施保持在国际安全标准之内，同时继续为伊朗的能源生产作出贡献。

title: 美国BWXT公司获400万美元Y-12锂加工设施概念设计合同
content:
美国BWXT公司获400万美元Y-12锂加工设施概念设计合同
2026-09-14 13:37 美国核电
近日，总部位于美国弗吉尼亚州林奇堡(Lynchburg)的核技术、核组件和核燃料制造企业BWX技术公司(BWX Technologies, Inc.，简称 BWXT)宣布，已获得美国能源部国家核安全局(DOE/NNSA)Y-12国家安全大楼(Y-12 National Security Complex)首个锂加工设施首个模块(Lithium Processing Facility)的概念设计合同。
据了解，Y-12国家安全大楼(Y-12 National Security Complex)，位于美国田纳西州橡树岭，由美国能源部旗下的国家核安全局(NNSA)管辖。核心业务围绕特种核材料的加工、处理和储存。现主要任务是生产、加工、储存和退役美国核武器中的富集铀部件(次级阶段组件)。负责为美国海军的核动力潜艇和航空母舰提供所需的核燃料(富集铀)以及回收和储存全球范围内的敏感核材料，防止核武器扩散。
在托卡马克(Tokamak)或激光聚变反应堆中，都需要使用锂包层(Lithium Blanket)来吸收中子并产生聚变燃料“氚”。BWXT 在 Y-12 积累的高纯度锂化学与高温熔融处理技术(Homogenization Technology)，在技术原理上可延伸应用于未来的商业核聚变能源工程。

美国能源部表示，计划向爱荷华州Palo(帕洛)地区的核设施提供最高20亿美元的资金支持，用于正式启动该核能项目。这一承诺是在爱荷华州州长金·雷诺兹领导核能研究工作组完成相关工作后正式提出的，标志着该州在推进核能发展方面迈出了实质性的一步。
据了解，Palo(帕洛)地区主要的核设施是位于美国亚利桑那州的 Palo Verde Generating Station(帕洛韦德核发电站)，地理位置位于亚利桑那州马里科帕县(Maricopa County)，在菲尼克斯(凤凰城)以西约50至55英里(近温特斯堡 Wintersburg/托诺帕 Tonopah 一带)。它是美国最大的核能发电设施，也是全美发电量名列前茅的核电站。拥有三个压水反应堆机组(Unit 1、Unit 2 和 Unit 3)，总发电容量超过4,000兆瓦，能够为亚利桑那州、加利福尼亚州、新墨西哥州及德克萨斯州西部的约400万居民提供清洁电力。
金·雷诺兹州长表示，帕洛核设施在投运后，将主要为全球范围内的数据中心提供电力供应。随着云计算和数字化转型的加速，数据中心对稳定电力的需求持续攀升，核能因此成为这一新兴领域的重要能源保障。该设施的建成，将有助于满足日益增长的电力需求，为数据产业的持续发展提供坚实支撑。
